title: Linux Hidden Files
description:
In Linux, configuration files and secret files that begin with a dot (.) are hidden from standard directory listings.

What command and flag did Swapnil demonstrate to list all files including hidden dotfiles in detailed long format?
hint: Use the 'ls' command with options for long format (-l) and all files (-a).

title: Print Working Directory
description:
When navigating deeply nested directories in the terminal, it is easy to lose track of your location in the filesystem tree.

Which 3-letter Linux command prints the full absolute path of your current working directory?

title: Displaying File Contents
description:
To inspect scripts, log files, or text notes without opening an interactive editor, Linux provides a command to concatenate and display file contents directly on screen.

What standard 3-letter command is used to read and output a file's content (e.g. ___ notes.txt)?
hint: Short for concatenate. Also rhymes with hat.

title: Searching Logs with Patterns
description:
In Karthik's session on log analysis, security analysts had to search through thousands of server log lines to isolate failed login attempts or errors.

Which command-line utility is used in Linux to search files or input streams for lines matching a specified pattern?

title: The Pipeline Operator
description:
A core philosophy of Unix/Linux is combining small tools together. You can take the output of one command and immediately feed it as the input to a second command.

What single character / operator is used between commands to create a pipeline (e.g. cat access.log ___ grep 404)?
hint: The vertical bar key, usually located above Enter (Shift + \).

title: Exposed Configuration Secrets
description:
In Shree's session on password exposures, a major cause of data breaches was developers accidentally committing environment config files containing database passwords and secret API keys to public Git repositories.

What is the standard name of this hidden configuration file (starting with a dot)?
hint: It starts with a dot and is short for 'environment'.

title: Insecure Password Storage
description:
Storing user passwords in clear, readable form without applying a cryptographic one-way hash function (like bcrypt or SHA-256) is a critical security vulnerability.

What is the cybersecurity term for passwords stored in unencrypted, readable text?
hint: Two words or one compound word: opposite of encrypted text.

title: Lookalike Domain Spoofing
description:
In Harshit's phishing session, attackers register domain names that look almost identical to genuine services by substituting letters with similar characters (e.g. paypa1.com or c0llege.edu) to deceive unsuspecting users.

What specific term describes this type of URL hijacking / domain attack?
hint: Combines 'typo' with the word for occupying property illegally.

title: Spotting the Phishing Link
description:
A student received an urgent email asking them to re-authenticate their account. Which of the following four URLs (A, B, C, or D) is the fraudulent phishing link?

[A] https://portal.college.edu/login
[B] https://c0llege.edu.verify-account.net/login
[C] https://github.com/workshop/notes
[D] https://mail.google.com

Enter the single letter (A, B, C, or D).
hint: Look closely at [B]: the actual domain is verify-account.net, not college.edu, and it uses 'c0llege' with a zero.

title: The ROT-13 Cipher
description:
In classic substitution ciphers, ROT-13 rotates each letter forward by 13 positions in the 26-letter alphabet.

Decode the 5-letter ciphertext below using this letter shift rule:
PLORE

Letter Shift Key: P → C, L → Y, O → B, R → E, E → R.

What 5-letter English tech word does it decode to?
hint: Apply the shift key to each letter in PLORE: P becomes C, L becomes Y, O becomes B, R becomes E, E becomes R.
